title: Optimal distance oracles that also report paths
formal: For positively weighted undirected graphs and integer \(k\ge2\), can a path-reporting distance oracle simultaneously use \(O(n^{1+1/k})\) space, have stretch \(2k-1\), and answer in constant overhead plus time proportional to the reported path?
definitions: Definitions and model details remain incomplete. Specify dependence on \(k\), word size, preprocessing, randomization and whether output cost counts edges or vertices.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated existence or universal proposition, or of its logical negation. This is a provisional candidate, not a completed benchmark specification. context: The supplied catalogue associates this question with Shiri Chechik. This is an editorial research connection, not a claim of authorship or a personal research agenda. why: This asks whether compact distance summaries can return actual routes without losing their best size and stretch guarantees.

import_provenance.original_title: Optimal distance oracles that also report paths
import_provenance.original_statement: For undirected positively weighted graphs, can a path-reporting distance oracle simultaneously achieve O(n^(1+1/k)) space, stretch 2k−1, and O(1) query overhead plus time proportional to the reported path? This asks to match Chechik's distance-only bounds while returning an actual approximate shortest path.
